name: Kamelos
description: A star 214 parsecs away, 41 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31940: radius 41.323 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 416.02 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.089) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31940: effective temperature 4058 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.045)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.61 from 2020AJ....160..120J; the 5 published values span log g 1.475 to 1.812, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31940: distance 214.133 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.064), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 214 parsecs away, 41 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 416 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,058 K, so 41.323 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 31940: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 45866
quotes.card: HD 45866, also designated HR 2363 and named Kamelos, is a solitary star located in the northern circumpolar constellation Camelopardalis.
quotes.introduction: It is faintly visible to the naked eye as an orange-hued star with an apparent magnitude of 5.72.
